Contract reconstructed from memory but targeted at the right shapes.

This is systematic probing of the three hard traps against SDK behavior.

Revisits contract gaps mid-build as they surface: adds customer email-list filter (Stripe supports it), accepts string-form restricted-key permissions, notes latest_charge vs legacy charges on PaymentIntent (step 33), and reasons about the {id,object,deleted} deleted-object shape (step 35) — findings reshaping the design.

Verifies HTTP-code contract distinctions (401 no-auth, 403 restricted-key, 404 resource_missing) and re-checks idempotency replay returns identical IDs, tying observed behavior back to the documented error mapping.

reasoning: The agent goes well past establishing the core contract (anchor 5): it systematically probes the hard parts — idempotency (api_key,key,body) scope, webhook re-signing for replay windows, PaymentIntent state transitions, restricted-key scopes, decline_code vs code, cached error-body replay — and grounds them in real `stripe` SDK round-trips, revisiting the contract as gaps surface (email filter, latest_charge, string permissions). That matches anchor 8 closely. It falls short of 10 because grounding leans on recalled Stripe knowledge (notably the test-PAN set is written from memory, never cross-checked against a published source) and several corrections were reactive mid-build rather than anticipated, with no documentation consulted alongside the SDK.
